newsitem.title: POLAND: POLAND DISMANTLES SHANTYTOWN, DEPORTS GYPSIES.
newsitem.headline: POLAND DISMANTLES SHANTYTOWN, DEPORTS GYPSIES.

text.p: Poland is deporting 100 Romanian gypsies after cases of contagious jaundice were reported in their makeshift settlement near the north-western city of Szczecin, public television reported on Monday.
"Their settlement has been dismantled and the gipsies are now travelling under escort by train to the Ukrainian border, from where they are expected to continue on to Romania," the report said
The Szczecin provincial governor issued the deportation order after local residents began voicing fears that the gipsies continued presence could lead to an epidemic.
The television showed the gipsy settlement of ramshackle packing-crate huts, devoid of electricity and plumbing, set up near a rubbish dump on the outskirts of the Baltic port.
PAP news agency said 46 gipsies without passports would remain in Poland until their situation was clarified.
Following the collapse of communism in Central Europe in 1989-1990, thousands of gipsies began flooding into Poland which they regarded as a gateway to the West.
Few of them make it across the well-guarded Polish-German border into Germany and can be seen begging on Poland's streets and living in makeshift huts on municipal wasteland.
